notes.blurb: Ochre cut stone under green tile, with dark timber between; an earth-built city that shows its stone and crowns it in a single strong colour.
notes.construction: Load-bearing sandstone laid in courses on a granite footing, dark oak posts and lintels framing the openings, red sandstone bands at sill and cornice.
notes.ground: Dry ochre stone and smooth paving; the ground is quarried and dressed rather than planted, and terraces are cut flat rather than followed.
notes.roofs: Green tile broken over two pitches, steep at the ridge and easing out to an upturned eave, hipped and gabled together at the ends; the civic halls carry the same tile in two tiers, shallow below and steep at the ridge.
notes.signature: The green roof against the ochre wall, repeated from the smallest house to the palace so the whole city reads as one built thing.
